name: Off Script
pitch: One big button picks a random title from all of Netflix US, and learns what you don't want, not what's trending.
problem: Recommendation feeds keep showing you more of the same.

stats.label: titles: the whole Netflix US catalog

features.title: Say why not
features.text: Each not-interested reason quietly lowers the odds of similar titles.
details: From not my genre to too long a commitment
Lowered, never ruled out, and fading by half in six months
One pick in five is a wildcard that ignores it all

screen.alt: A pick, Charlotte, a Japanese series rated 8.2, beside the Why not panel of reasons: genre, tone, look and feel, origin and mood

features.title: Keep track
features.text: Mark a pick as watching, watched, maybe later or not interested.
details: Lists for later, passed, in progress and watched
Synced to your Google account when you sign in

screen.alt: A pick card with its rating, a summary, links to Netflix, IMDb and TMDB, and buttons to mark it

features.title: Pick by mood or place
features.text: Choose categories around the button: Asia, Dark, Laughs, Era and more.
details: Within a group choices widen; across groups they narrow
Films, series or both, and a minimum score

features.title: Always current
features.text: The catalog refreshes itself on the 1st of every month.
details: All picking happens in your browser

screens.alt: Off Script: a big Hit me button ringed by categories like Asia, Europe, Dark, Heart, Laughs and Mood, with filters for length and score
screens.caption: One button, and the categories around it

facts.builtWith: One HTML file and a catalog
